title: Free AI whiteboard: sticky notes sorted with your team · {name}
description: Brainstorm, run a retrospective or plan by weeks on a whiteboard of sticky notes: write with your team, and let AI sort the notes into sections. Free.
h1: Write your notes together, and let AI sort them while you watch.
acts: and let AI sort them while you watch.
lede: Ask {name} for a brainstorm, a retrospective or a plan by weeks, and it makes a board of short notes in named sections. Everyone drags, writes and draws on the same board, live. When notes pile up, {name} sorts them, and you accept or reject each change.
cta: Try it with a sample retrospective
facts: One board, the same for everyone
try.ask: Make a whiteboard for the retrospective of our open day. Went well: more visitors than last year, the guided tours were full, parents liked the students’ stands. To change: the queue at the entrance, signs were hard to find, no leaflets left by noon. To try: booking the tours ahead, a map on every door.

pane.asked: Here is what the AI would do. Each change carries a yellow corner: accept them, reject them, or press {before} to see the board without them.

exact.title: Its changes wait for you.
exact.why: A board is a team’s thinking: nothing on it should move behind your back. What the AI changes is marked and counted, and yours to accept or reject.
exact.cards: Each note the AI moved or wrote carries a yellow corner. Accept or reject them one by one, or all at once.
{before} shows the board as it was, without the changes that wait. Nothing is lost until you decide.
The AI sorts and writes notes. It doesn’t touch your drawings, and leaves what you placed by hand on the open board where it is.
where.title: Where your board lives.
where.why: On your devices. Shared only with the people you invite, each in their own {name}.
where.cards: Your board is plain files in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
When you ask, its notes go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
Others see the board only once you invite them to work on it. Their changes merge with yours, note by note.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Making or sorting a whiteboard needs an AI in the cloud or a plan you pay for: the AI on this computer reads a board, and doesn’t change one.
To write on a board with you, each person opens it in their own {name}. A link anyone can open shows a copy to read, not the board itself.
{name} places what the AI makes: you can’t ask for a note in a given spot. Drag it there yourself.
The AI reads the notes, the sections and the arrows between them. It doesn’t read drawings, and makes neither drawings nor arrows.
{name} can be wrong. A note sorted into the wrong section is one drag away from the right one.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for.
Is it like a wall of sticky notes?
Yes: short notes you drag around, in sections you name, with texts, arrows and freehand drawings, on a board that pans and zooms. And an AI that sorts the notes when you ask.
Can several people use it at once?
Yes. Share it to work on it together: everyone sees the same board, where the others point, and each change as it is made.
Does it work on a phone?
Yes. A narrow screen opens on the lanes, one section at a time, with the same notes. The board itself pans and zooms with two fingers.
Can I get my notes out?
Yes: as a picture of the board, or as a table of its notes by section, to copy, to print or to download as Excel or CSV.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: the notes are written in yours, and a board made in a right-to-left language starts from the right.
end.title: Try it with the open day’s retrospective.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered as soon as you choose an AI. Then ask for your own board.
